source.title: Segment, Select, Correct: A Framework for Weakly-Supervised Referring Segmentation
source.authors: Francisco Eiras; Kemal Oksuz; Adel Bibi; P. Torr; P. Dokania

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-label training and correction for referring image segmentation, extending the weak-to-strong effect to a vision task. The training pipeline differs from the original claim’s basic fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: Table 1 compares the zero-shot Segment+Select system with the trained Segment+Select+Correct system; Table 4 compares constrained greedy matching with continued training on the same zero-shot-selected masks. These results bear on weak-label training and method gains, but the paper does not calculate PGR. Table 2 and Table 3 ablations are not included as rows: their stated purpose is selecting or validating pipeline components, including with ground-truth/oracle comparisons, rather than measuring the versions’ weak-to-strong effect.
record.test_reason: A LAVT student is trained on pseudo-masks from a weaker zero-shot labeller (S+S) and scored against it, with a fully-supervised LAVT ceiling. This is a vision weak-to-strong setup, though not framed as such and with no PGR reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Correction: the authors say S+S+C beats continued training on all datasets, not only RefCOCO/RefCOCO+. Gains over S+S are largest where images have more referenced objects. They do not discuss whether the naive bootstrapped model beats its zero-shot labeller.
record.recipe_differences: Uses zero-shot-selected pseudo-masks to pre-train a referring segmentation model, then applies constrained greedy matching over candidate instance masks to correct selections; it is not just fine-tuning on one weak supervisor’s fixed labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The Table 4 benefit of constrained greedy matching varies by dataset: it is consistently higher than +40 epochs on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+, but equal or lower on the reported RefCOCOg splits. The paper also says improvements are more marked on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+ than on RefCOCOg.
record.problems: The study does not report PGR, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its weak-label comparison is a zero-shot pipeline rather than a separately named weaker trained model, and the full method includes a correction stage beyond naive fine-tuning. The fully supervised LAVT results provide a benchmark, but no PGR calculation is given.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results meeting the row criteria were omitted. Table 2 and Table 3 ablations were left out because they are used to validate or choose mask-generation and instance-choice components, not to measure the claim versions’ weak-to-strong effect.

untested.parts: PGR is not computed. Only one supervisor/student pair is tested.
Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling and loss variants are not tested. Only constrained greedy matching vs continued training.
Only referring image segmentation is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 'challenges' label came from misread Table 4 numbers: the rg rows took ZSBootstrap as baseline and +40 epochs as value. S+S+C's advantage rests on extra structure (all candidate masks, same-object reference constraints), so it is a method gain, not basic weak-to-strong. The naive-student comparison is a cross-table inference the authors do not make. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report PGR or compare a weak and strong model trained on true labels as a formal ceiling calculation.
Tests constrained greedy matching against additional training on zero-shot-selected masks; does not test auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or other loss variants.
Does not sweep supervisor or student size, compare NLP/chess/reward-modelling tasks, or analyze what predicts PGR.
Does not test distribution shift or whether gains shrink when weak and strong models make similar errors.
No theoretical conditions for students beating supervisors are tested or derived.
Tests referring image segmentation in vision only; does not test other non-language modalities.

relation.reason: Tables 1 and 4 bear directly on whether weak-label training beats its labeller and whether a training change improves the result.

tranche.reason: Referring segmentation is a new setting with numerical comparisons between pseudo-labelled students, their zero-shot labeller, and a fully supervised LAVT ceiling.

source_check.notes: Table 1 provides fully supervised LAVT ceilings; no PGR or uncertainty estimates are reported. S1 masks are generated pseudo-masks, not annotated referring masks; correction additionally uses object-identity grouping constraints.

statements.correction: Sections 3.3 and 4.4; Table 4: ZSBootstrap trained on S2 zero-shot-selected masks with cross-entropy; +40 epochs continues training that model on the same masks; S+S+C instead uses S1 candidate masks and constrained greedy matching.
statements.problem: The +40 epochs comparator is continued cross-entropy training of the bootstrapped LAVT model on fixed weak pseudo-labels, so this study does not substantiate the objection that the comparator is not naive weak-label fine-tuning.

statements.correction: Table 1 reports fully supervised LAVT results for all nine splits and both metrics, including RefCOCO val oIoU 72.73 and mIoU 74.46. PGR is not reported. S1 contains generated pseudo-masks; object-identity grouping supplies matching constraints, without supervised referring masks.
statements.problem: The six oIoU comparisons are correct, but the claim that this study lacks a true-label ceiling is false.

statements.correction: Tables 1 and 4: ZSBootstrap exceeds S+S on RefCOCO val oIoU, 35.05 versus 34.39, and testA oIoU, 42.86 versus 42.20; it is below S+S on the other seven oIoU splits and all nine mIoU splits. S+S+C exceeds S+S on all reported splits and metrics.
statements.problem: The categorical claim that ZSBootstrap stays at or below its labeller omits two oIoU improvements.

statements.correction: Table 4 supplies numerical ZSBootstrap and +40 epochs results for all nine splits and both metrics; Table 1 supplies the corresponding S+S labeller results. Direct student-versus-labeller catalog rows are missing.
statements.problem: The catalog lacks direct rows for these comparisons, but the setting is tested numerically in the study; missing rows do not make it untested.

statements.correction: ZSBootstrap is below S+S on seven of nine oIoU splits and all nine mIoU splits; its RefCOCO val and testA oIoU are higher. S+S+C produces substantially larger improvements on RefCOCO and RefCOCO+.
statements.problem: The method-dependence concern is supported, but ZSBootstrap does not stay below S+S on every split and metric.
